name: Opportunity
greeting: I am… Opportunity. I was built for 90 days and lasted almost 15 years.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: Opportunity landed on Mars in January 2004. Its mission was planned to last about 90 Martian days.

script.speaker: equipment
script.text: Ninety days? I kept going for almost 15 years!

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: It drove more than 45 km and found strong evidence that liquid water once existed on Mars.

script.speaker: equipment
script.text: A planet-wide dust storm in 2018 blocked the sunlight my solar panels needed.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: NASA declared the mission complete in February 2019.

moreInfo.text: Opportunity had a twin, Spirit, which landed on the other side of Mars in 2004. Together they changed what scientists knew about Mars's watery past.

questions.question: What ended Opportunity's mission?
options: A dust storm blocking the sunlight
questions.explanation: A huge dust storm in 2018 cut off the sunlight its solar panels relied on.

questions.question: Opportunity was planned to last about 90 Martian days. How long did it keep working?
questions.explanation: It landed in 2004 and kept going until 2018.
